## Best practices[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#best-practices)

These are the rules ADVISOR holds itself to, the short version for people who use ADVISOR and people who add to it, with the test that enforces each rule where there is one.

Tags: Enforced (code or CI stops the bad outcome), Documented (written down only), Not yet (a gap).

### Approve it by name, and review the config like code[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#approve-it-by-name-and-review-the-config-like-code)

`.mcp.json` starts a program on whoever opens the project. Keep it out of git (this repo ignores it); `advisor install` warns when you have not. Enforced (warning).

### Treat answers as data[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#treat-answers-as-data)

Every result says where it came from and that it is reference text. PROCTOR in CI decides pass or fail; ADVISOR never does. Enforced (labels), Documented (the rule).

### Run it in development only[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-it-in-development-only)

It refuses to start unless `ADVISOR_ENABLED` is set and refuses in production. Enforced.

### Keep secrets out of what you ask[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#keep-secrets-out-of-what-you-ask)

Do not paste tokens into prompts. Audit logs hold hashes, never arguments, and PROCTOR output is redacted. Enforced.

### Run Boost beside it in Laravel apps[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-boost-beside-it-in-laravel-apps)

Boost knows the framework, ADVISOR knows WSU. They do not overlap. Documented.

### Read-only first[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#read-only-first)

Every tool states all four hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world). A tool that writes is left out unless `ADVISOR_READ_ONLY` is turned off, and that switch beats tool groups. Enforced (contract test).

### Narrow tools, closed schemas[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#narrow-tools-closed-schemas)

No tool takes a command, a URL or a free path. Schemas set `additionalProperties: false`, and arguments are validated again on our side. Enforced (contract test).

### Run other programs the safe way[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#run-other-programs-the-safe-way)

Fixed program, argument array, allowlisted environment, a timeout, and no shell. Paths are resolved and must stay inside the project root. Enforced.

### Keep stdout clean[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#keep-stdout-clean)

Only protocol lines go to stdout; logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr. Enforced (subprocess test).

### Strip invisible characters[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#strip-invisible-characters)

The TAG block, zero-width and bidirectional controls are removed from everything served and rejected in tool metadata. Enforced (contract test).

### Load modules from a manifest only[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#load-modules-from-a-manifest-only)

From the `Waynestate\` namespace, implementing `Module`. Never scan. Enforced.

### Serve from verified data[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#serve-from-verified-data)

Bundled content is checked against a SHA-256 manifest at start-up and in CI; a mismatch stops the server. Enforced.

### Review any change to the tool list[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#review-any-change-to-the-tool-list)

`tools/list` is snapshotted; a changed description is a reviewed diff. Enforced (snapshot test).

### Cite sources and date[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#cite-sources-and-date)

Policy answers carry the day they were worked out for and the file they came from. Enforced.

### Not yet[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#not-yet)

- Testing on a native Windows PHP (the SDK has no Windows CI), and the MCP Inspector in CI.
- Signing of any state handed back to a client (no tool needs it in 0.1).
- A threat model mapped to OWASP and NIST; a full-capture audit mode.

### Related[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html#related)

- [Proof](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)
- [Safety](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/safety.html)
- [Changelog](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html)

Source: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html

## Commands[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands)

Every command the `advisor` CLI takes, and what it does.

### Running a command[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#running-a-command)

Run any command with `php vendor/bin/advisor <command>`. This is one PHP command, not a shell script, so it works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. The `mcp` command is started by your MCP client, not by you.

```
php vendor/bin/advisor mcp                          # serve over stdio (your client starts this)
php vendor/bin/advisor install [--client=claude] [--write] [--force] [--path=.]
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify               # check the bundled content against its manifest
php vendor/bin/advisor content:generate [--sources=<dir>] [--check]
php vendor/bin/advisor stack-parts [--write=<readme>] [--check=<readme>]
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor [--json]              # check the install when the server does not show up
```

Stdout carries only protocol messages. Logs, warnings and stray output go to stderr, so a client never sees garbage.

### Commands[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#commands-1)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/advisor doctor` | Check the install: PHP, the bundled content, the client config, and the server. |
| `bin/advisor install` | Print (or with --write, write) the MCP client config that starts ADVISOR. |
| `bin/advisor mcp` | Serve ADVISOR to an MCP client over stdio (started by the client, not by hand). |
| `bin/advisor stack-parts` | Render the stack parts table from the seed; write or check the marked block in a README. |
| `bin/advisor content:generate` | Rebuild the bundled content from the stack repositories (--check only compares). |
| `bin/advisor content:verify` | Check the bundled content against its manifest. |

#### `bin/advisor doctor` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-doctor)

Check the install: PHP, the bundled content, the client config, and the server.

Usage: `bin/advisor doctor [--json]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print the findings as JSON. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor install` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-install)

Print (or with --write, write) the MCP client config that starts ADVISOR.

Usage: `bin/advisor install [-c|--client CLIENT] [--write] [--force] [--path PATH]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--client=VALUE` | claude, warriorgpt, cursor, vscode or codex. | `claude` |
| `--write` | Write the file in the project instead of printing it. |  |
| `--force` | Replace an existing, different "advisor" entry. |  |
| `--path=VALUE` | Project folder to write into. | `.` |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor mcp` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-mcp)

Serve ADVISOR to an MCP client over stdio (started by the client, not by hand).

Usage: `bin/advisor mcp`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor stack-parts` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-stack-parts)

Render the stack parts table from the seed; write or check the marked block in a README.

Usage: `bin/advisor stack-parts [--write WRITE] [--check CHECK]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--write=VALUE` | Replace the block between the stack-parts markers in this file (repeatable) |  |
| `--check=VALUE` | Exit 1 when the block in this file is stale (repeatable) |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor content:generate` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-content-generate)

Rebuild the bundled content from the stack repositories (--check only compares).

Usage: `bin/advisor content:generate [-s|--sources SOURCES] [--check]`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-s`, `--sources=VALUE` | Folder that holds the stack repositories (creed, proctor, wayne-ui, ...). Default: ADVISOR_STACK_DIR. |  |
| `--check` | Exit 1 when the bundle differs from what the sources produce; write nothing. |  |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### `bin/advisor content:verify` [#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#bin-advisor-content-verify)

Check the bundled content against its manifest.

Usage: `bin/advisor content:verify`

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--silent` | Do not output any message |  |

#### Options every command accepts[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#options-every-command-accepts)

| Option | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | Display help for the given command. When no command is given display help for the list command |  |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Only errors are displayed. All other output is suppressed |  |
| \`-v | -vv | -vvv`, `--verbose\` |
| `-V`, `--version` | Display this application version |  |
| `--ansi` | Force (or disable --no-ansi) ANSI output |  |
| `--no-ansi` | Negate the "--ansi" option |  |
| `-n`, `--no-interaction` | Do not ask any interactive question |  |

### Exit codes[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#exit-codes)

- `content:generate --check` exits `1` on drift, when the bundled content no longer matches the source repos.
- `doctor` exits `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON.
- `composer content:drift` exits `1` when `data/` no longer matches the stack repos, or when `ADVISOR_STACK_DIR` is not set.

### Related[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html#related)

## Configuration[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#configuration)

ADVISOR reads the process environment only, never a file. This page lists every variable with its default and its meaning, and the placeholders are in `.env.example`. Nothing in 0.1 needs a secret, key, certificate, token or host, so every setting is optional.

### Environment variables[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#environment-variables)

| Variable | Meaning | Default | Read in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG | A file for a one-line-per-call audit log: time, tool, a hash of the arguments, outcome, duration. Arguments are hashed, never written. | off | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN | Where `upgrade_path` finds Booster when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own: the path to booster's `bin/booster` (or a `booster.phar`). The app's own `vendor/bin/booster` always wins. | none | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT | Seconds before a Booster plan is stopped (1 to 900). A plan is local and fast, so the default is shorter than a PROCTOR run. | `60` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_ENABLED | Must be `1` or `true`, or the server refuses to start. `advisor install` sets it in the client config. | off | src/Command/ClientConfig.php |
| ADVISOR_ENV | `production` or `prod` always refuses to start. | `APP_ENV`, then `local` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_GROUPS | Comma list of tool groups to offer (`stack`, `proctor`, `booster`). See below for what each group may start. | all | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_LOG_LEVEL | Log level on stderr (`debug` to `emergency`). | `warning` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_MAX_CHARS | Largest piece of text one doc call returns (1000 to 45000). | `20000` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_MODULES_FILE | An extra module manifest (see "Modules"). | none | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_PRIVATE_DENYLIST | A file (kept outside the repo) with private strings to strip from the bundle; used by `content:generate` and the public-posture test. See "Releasing". | none | src/Content/Denylist.php |
| ADVISOR_PROCTOR_TIMEOUT | Seconds before a PROCTOR run is stopped (1 to 900). | `120` | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT | The folder `run_proctor_check` may look inside. Paths outside it are refused. | the working directory | src/Command/DoctorCommand.php |
| ADVISOR_READ_ONLY | Set to `0` or `false` to allow tools that write. None exist in 0.1. Read-only wins over `ADVISOR_GROUPS`. | on | src/Config.php |
| ADVISOR_STACK_DIR | Folder holding the sibling stack repos; used only by `content:generate`. | none | src/Command/ContentGenerateCommand.php |

### Example[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.html#example)

A short example, with placeholder values:

```bash
ADVISOR_ENABLED=1
ADVISOR_ENV=local
ADVISOR_PROJECT_ROOT=/path/to/your/app
ADVISOR_AUDIT_LOG=/path/to/advisor-audit.log
```

`advisor install` sets `ADVISOR_ENABLED` in the client config for you.

Warning

A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

## Proof[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#proof)

This page walks through `composer ci`, the one command that proves the build, and what each step of it proves.

The same command runs on GitLab and GitHub.

### The command[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#the-command)

```
composer ci
```

No PHP on your machine? Use Docker:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2.10.3 sh -c "composer install --no-interaction && composer ci"
```

### composer validate --strict[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#composer-validate-strict)

Runs `composer validate --strict` on the package metadata.

### content:verify[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#content-verify)

Runs `php bin/advisor content:verify`, which checks the bundled content against its manifest. CI cannot see the sibling repositories, so `composer ci` runs `content:verify`, which needs none of them.

### stack-parts --check=README.md[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#stack-parts-check-readme-md)

Runs `php bin/advisor stack-parts --check=README.md`, which proves the parts table in the README still matches `generator/projects.seed.json`.

### PHPUnit[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#phpunit)

Runs `phpunit`. Tests drive the real SDK server in-process with a small MCP client, snapshot `tools/list`, and start `bin/advisor mcp` as a subprocess to prove stdout stays clean.

Tip

To accept an intended change to the tool list, run `ADVISOR_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 vendor/bin/phpunit`, then review and commit the diff.

### Pint[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#pint)

Runs `pint --test`, the style check.

### site:agent-ready-check[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#site-agent-ready-check)

Fails when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here.

### PHPStan[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#phpstan)

Runs `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G`: level 8, Pinstripe's raw preset, included from `vendor/waynestate/pinstripe`.

### composer audit[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#composer-audit)

Runs `composer audit`.

### docs:check[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#docs-check)

Fails when `site/docs/` is stale or a docs page has a broken link, block or nav entry.

### Related[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.html#related)

- [Best practices](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/best-practices.html)
- [Commands](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/commands.html)

## Troubleshooting[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

This page lists the failure symptoms ADVISOR's own docs describe, with the cause, the fix and the command that checks it.

#### The advisor server is not in the list[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-advisor-server-is-not-in-the-list)

You added the config, opened the project, and the `advisor` server is not in the list.

**Cause.** One of four things keeps a server from appearing:

- **php**: the PHP on your machine satisfies ADVISOR's own `composer.json` (8.3 or newer).
- **content**: the bundled `data/` still matches its manifest.
- **client:claude**, **client:warriorgpt**, **client:cursor**, **client:vscode**: each client's MCP config: is the file there, does it have the `advisor` entry, and is the script it points at in the project? A missing file is a warning, not a failure; you only need the one client you use.
- **mcp**: the server actually starts. Doctor boots it in-process and asks for its tools.

**Fix.** Run doctor and fix anything it reports as a `fail`. A `fail` is something to fix; a `warn` is something you may not care about.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

The exit code is `0` when nothing failed and `1` when something did; `--json` prints the findings as JSON.

#### The server refuses to start because it is not enabled[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-because-it-is-not-enabled)

**Cause.** `ADVISOR_ENABLED` defaults to off. It must be `1` or `true`, or the server refuses to start.

**Fix.** Set `ADVISOR_ENABLED=1` in the client config's environment. `advisor install` sets it in the client config.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

#### The server refuses to start in production[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-in-production)

**Cause.** `ADVISOR_ENV` reads `APP_ENV`, then `local`. `production` or `prod` always refuses to start.

**Fix.** Run ADVISOR in development only. It refuses to start in production by design.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

#### A bad setting stops the server[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-bad-setting-stops-the-server)

**Cause.** A bad value stops the server with a message on stderr. It does not guess.

**Fix.** Read the message on stderr and correct the value. ADVISOR reads the process environment only, never a file.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor doctor
```

#### The server refuses to start because a content file fails its hash[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-server-refuses-to-start-because-a-content-file-fails-its-hash)

**Cause.** The bundled `data/` is verified at start-up against `data/manifest.json` (a SHA-256 for every file). If a file does not match, the server refuses to start rather than serve it.

**Fix.** Regenerate the bundle from the sibling stack repositories with `content:generate`, then verify it.

**Check.**

```bash
php vendor/bin/advisor content:verify
```

## Upgrading[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page walks through each released version of ADVISOR and what changed, so you can see whether a new version affects your app.

### Unreleased[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#unreleased)

A docs site built from `docs/` is added and checked in `composer ci`. The bundled data is resynced several times with the stack main branches of 2026-11-03, picking up changes in SESAME, HELMET, PROCTOR, Pinstripe, Sourdough, Squire, WELD, Booster, Preflight, Drawbridge, Rollcall, and others. ADVISOR's own version reads 0.1.5.

### \[0.1.5\] - 2026-11-03[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-5-2026-11-03)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- The deploy layer requires HELMET ^0.3 and PROCTOR ^0.4 (locked at 0.3.0 and 0.4.0) and sets minimum-stability to stable, which clears PROCTOR 0.4's new minimum-stability warning. HELMET 0.3 reads an empty `HELMET_PROXIES=` as trust nobody; the front page sets only the `citadel` preset, so nothing changes for it.
- The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.5.0 (updated `base-fallback.Dockerfile`, `scripts/release.sh` and `scripts/parity.ps1`).
- The bundled data is resynced with the 2026-11-03 releases: Booster 1.8.0, Preflight 0.1.4, PROCTOR 0.4.0, Pinstripe 0.1.2, CREED 0.1.6, Rollcall 0.1.9, HELMET 0.3.0, SESAME 0.4.0, Drawbridge 0.1.1, Sourdough 0.1.5, Squire 0.5.0 and WELD 0.1.2, and with each project's main since the last pass.
- One Playbook settings resolver (`Waynestate\Advisor\Playbook\Settings`, ADR-0018) is added. `playbook_lookup` now answers from `.env.playbook` when the package is not installed (same output shape).
- `.env.playbook` is git-ignored; the agent-ready files (`site/llms.txt`, `site/llms-full.txt`) are regenerated.
- Docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

### \[0.1.4\] - 2026-11-03[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-4-2026-11-03)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.

### \[0.1.3\] - 2026-11-02[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3-2026-11-02)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- Hand-written guides are bundled from `generator/guides/` and served as `advisor://guide/<slug>`; the first guide is "Connect to Oracle on Citadel".
- `policy_lookup` returns `latest_patch`; the bundled docs drop hero images, badges and GIFs.
- WayneUI's migration guide (MIGRATING.md) is bundled as the `migrating` doc, and every project entry carries its version when it publishes one (composer.json, else package.json, else the newest CHANGELOG heading).
- A one-line `claude mcp add` and a Docker `.mcp.json` for machines without PHP are documented.
- `composer content:drift` and an optional CI job fail when `data/` no longer matches the sibling repos.
- The deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local `.env.squire` file is now git-ignored).

### \[0.1.2\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-2-2026-10-29)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- An agent-ready site (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt) is added from Squire's kit.
- The `playbook_lookup` tool answers "what is the value of X?" for WSU shared values. An environment variable of the same name wins, then the private `waynestate/playbook` package (Playbook) supplies the rest; without it the tool says how to get it instead of failing. Keys that look like secrets (ending in SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN or KEY) are refused. `waynestate/playbook` is suggested, never required.
- Docs copies are resynced; proof results now live on the proof site.
- Project names are written as words except acronyms.
- Stale capability claims in the site and docs are fixed.

### \[0.1.1\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

No breaking changes are marked for this release.

- The `owner_of` tool answers "which project owns X?" from a new bundled `data/ownership.json` table (sourced from `generator/ownership.json`, verified by `content:verify`). Fuzzy match: every word of the topic must appear in a row's topic or role; a no-match answer lists every known topic.
- `upgrade_path` moves from the `stack` group to a new `booster` group, so `ADVISOR_GROUPS=stack` offers reference tools only and never starts a program. `ADVISOR_GROUPS` now accepts `stack`, `proctor` and `booster`.
- PHPStan includes Pinstripe's `raw.neon` preset (`waynestate/pinstripe` 0.1.0 as a dev dependency) instead of a hand copy of its settings; two docblocks were tightened to satisfy the preset's method-signature checks. Pint already used the `per` preset, so `pint.json` is unchanged.

### \[0.1.0\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0-2026-10-29)

This is the first release, so there is nothing to break.

- Read-only MCP server over stdio (`php vendor/bin/advisor mcp`) on the official `mcp/sdk` 0.9.0, speaking both the legacy `initialize` handshake and the 2026-07-28 per-request form.
- Seven tools: `list_projects`, `get_project_status`, `read_project_docs`, `policy_lookup`, `list_stack_rules`, `run_proctor_check`, `upgrade_path`. Resources `advisor://policy` and `advisor://creed/<chapter>`. Prompts `orient_me` and `plan_upgrade`.
- `upgrade_path` plans the app's PHP and/or Laravel upgrade, one supported hop at a time, by running Booster's read-only `plan` (never `run`) against the bundled policy. New settings `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_TIMEOUT` (default 60) and `ADVISOR_BOOSTER_BIN` (fallback when the app has no `vendor/bin/booster` of its own).
- Bundled, hash-verified content (CREED handbook and policy, project docs, the WayneUI markup contract) with a generator, `content:generate --check` and `content:verify`.
- `advisor install` for Claude, WarriorGPT, Cursor, VS Code (written) and Codex (printed).
- Laravel adapter on `laravel/mcp` (`php artisan mcp:start advisor`), so ADVISOR runs beside Laravel Boost.
- Safety: off unless enabled, refuses production, read-only by default, path confinement, allowlisted child environment, redaction, invisible-character stripping, manifest-only module loading, argument-hash audit log.
- `composer ci`: validate, content verify, PHPUnit, Pint, PHPStan level 8 (Pinstripe settings), audit. CI files for GitLab (Preflight 0.1.0) and GitHub.

### Taking a new version[#](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#taking-a-new-version)

ADVISOR is on Packagist: `composer require --dev waynestate/advisor:^0.1`. No extra repository needed.

The command is then `php vendor/bin/advisor`. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is one PHP command and not a shell script.
